column2: I am shopping for good food, sealed drinks and treats for the household. Show me what is fresh.
The salon is debating which soda deserves proper glassware. I think the answer is all of them.
My friends keep asking where I found these drinks. I prefer a reliable shop to an impressive address.
Someone served ordinary noodles at a formal dinner and called them a rediscovered tradition.
The latest fashion is to praise simple food in very complicated language.
The galleries are preparing another opening. Everyone remembers the refreshments first.
I am organizing a small evening gathering. Small is a surprisingly flexible word to my guests.
Our cook wants to know who supplies your ingredients. I told her to ask you herself.
One of my neighbors collects empty bottles. I am helping with the enjoyable half of that hobby.
A tasting party is a wonderful way to discover that nobody agrees about sweetness.
The upper lifts are crowded today. I would rather wait here with a decent drink.
I'll come by tomorrow. I'm looking for {0}.
That's {0} credits at the night markets. Take the lot now for {1}.
Suit yourself. It's all on the night-market shelves, at full price.
Money's tight, I know. I'll come by again in a week.
No room on your counters for all this. Clear some space and I'll come back.
A piece went astray, so {0} credits off.
Morning. I fit out shop kitchens, and yours could use a start.
A board, a bowl, two recipe books and ingredients for your first dishes.
Open your kitchen worktop. Book and ingredients in the INPUT, tool in its slot, then pick the dish.
Cold dishes: work them a few times, then finish. Overdo it and they spoil. Signal Sorghum and Kilnseed in the bowl make Ration Crunch.
You sell water. Shame to sell it plain when it could be a drink.
A Manual Bottling Kit, its handbook, four glass bottles and two each of Reserve, Cordial and Tonic concentrate.
Open the kit. Handbook, one concentrate, an empty bottle and clean water in the INPUT. Pick the drink and fill.
No power needed, but the water must be 99% pure. One concentrate, one bottle.
That Hydroponic System of yours can grow more than nutrifruit.
Two seed packs, apples and cabbage. Three seeds in each.
Plant a seed in the grower as you would nutrifruit, and harvest when it's ripe.
Save seeds from a healthy harvest and you won't need me again.
I breed rats. Meat, pets, the odd prize coat. You've room for a cage.
A cage, a breeding pair and my keeper's notes.
Put both rats in the cage and keep them fed. They'll breed on their own.
Keep the best young for breeding and sell the rest. The notes explain the traits.
Moisture Farms all over the shop floor? I can tidy that up.
A compact wall depot in its crate, and a Throughput Core.
Joe Wild fits the crate in a back-room bay, fitting included. Dock your water machines in the depot.
The core goes in a machine's module slot and speeds it up.
You've a Chem Finisher and nothing to put through it. I bring dry stock up from the docks.
Three cylinders: two of Dock Chalk, one of Emberwake. Three portions each.
Cylinder in the finisher, pick the matching product, press Finish.
The workshop handbook lists more uses for the stock. Mind who sees you selling it.
You've drinks on your shelves. Mix them and you've got cocktails.
A bar rail, a mixing glass with spoon, the cocktail book and two spirits to start.
Measure 50 mL of each spirit into the mixing glass and stir. That's a Railway Double.
Stir anything fizzy. A shaker opens up the rest of the book.
A tank pays its way in a shop. I breed tilapia.
A breeding pair of tilapia and my tank notes.
A fish tank, a breeding pair of tilapia and my tank notes.
Put them in the tank with clean water and power, and keep them fed.
They lay on their own. The notes cover clutches and colour lines.
Your kitchen's outgrown the worktop. I sell production galleys.
The Dockside Production Galley, its workshop recipe book and a supply case to get going.
Book and ingredients in its INPUT and a charged cell. It works through the night.
Start with flour: one nutrifruit makes two Nutrifruit flour. There's nutrifruit in the case.
Cans travel and don't break. I sell the Fizzworks Canner.
The canner, its recipe book, four cola syrups and four empty cans.
Book, syrup and a can in the INPUT, plus clean water and a charged cell. Pick Quay Cola and fill.
One syrup fills one can. Fresh-fruit sodas fill four at a time.
Your cellar's empty. I sell the bench that fills it.
The Cellar Bench, the brewing book, and bottles and culture for a first wine.
Nutrifruit, sweetener, culture, an empty bottle and clean water. Load one batch and leave it three nights.
Wine becomes brandy on the same bench. The book shows how.
